question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

She ventured to go back to the tree of the (tryst), the mulberry with the shining white fruit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Separation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tryst (noun) means a private, pre-arranged meeting, especially between lovers. (गुप्त मिलन / मुलाकात)

◦ Its antonym is Separation, meaning the act of parting or being apart. (अलगाव / विच्छेद)

◦ Correct: She ventured to go back to the tree of the separation, the mulberry with the shining white fruit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rendezvous – an appointed meeting place; a direct synonym of tryst, not an antonym.

• Engagement – a formal arrangement to meet or a betrothal; again close in meaning to tryst.

• Date – a social/romantic appointment; a synonym of tryst.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tryst: rendezvous, assignation, date, meeting.

• Antonyms of tryst: separation, parting, farewell, split.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Her notoriety increased after she single-______ shot down a Rhodesian army helicopter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. handedly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the prefix “single-”, so the required word must form the fixed adverb single-handedly, meaning done alone, without any help. (अकेले / बिना किसी की मदद के)

◦ Only “handedly” combines with “single-” to give a meaningful English word.

◦ Correct: Her notoriety increased after she single-handedly shot down a Rhodesian army helicopter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• “single-dose” is a medical adjective (a single-dose vaccine) and cannot modify the verb “shot down”.

• “single-plainly” is not an English word.

• “single-stranded” describes DNA/RNA or rope, not a person’s action.

NOTE

• Similar hyphenated adverbs/adjectives: single-minded (determined), open-handed (generous), high-handed (domineering), even-handed (fair).

• Notoriety = fame for something bad. (कुख्याति)

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Drive two blocks and turn right at the traffic lights.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is an imperative joined by “and”: “Drive … and turn …”, so the bare base verb turn is correct (parallel with “Drive”).

◦ Right here is an adverb of direction (turn right/left) – it is never changed to “rightly”, which means “correctly/justly”.

◦ The preposition at is used for a specific point such as traffic lights, a crossing or a corner.

◦ Correct: Drive two blocks and turn right at the traffic lights.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “turn right in” – “in” is used for enclosed spaces/areas, not for a point like traffic lights.

• Option 3 “turns right at” – the ‑s form breaks the imperative and the parallelism with “Drive”.

• Option 4 “turn rightly at” – “rightly” means “justifiably” and cannot show direction.

NOTE

• at = exact point (at the corner, at the signal); on = surface/street (on Mall Road); in = enclosed area (in the city).

• Adverb pairs to remember: hard/hardly, late/lately, near/nearly, right/rightly – the ‑ly forms have completely different meanings.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Enervate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Devitalize.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Enervate (verb) means to weaken, to drain of energy or vitality. (निर्बल करना / शक्तिहीन करना)

◦ Devitalize means exactly the same – to take away vitality or strength.

◦ Correct: The long march in the summer heat enervated (devitalized) the soldiers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Invigorate – to give energy or strength; an antonym of enervate.

• Arouse – to awaken or stir up a feeling; the opposite idea of draining energy.

• Boost – to increase or improve; also an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of enervate: debilitate, sap, exhaust, weaken, drain, fatigue.

• Antonyms of enervate: invigorate, energise, fortify, strengthen, rejuvenate.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A person holding conversational belief especially in matter of religion
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Orthodox.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Orthodox describes a person who follows conventional, traditionally accepted beliefs, especially in religion. (रूढ़िवादी / परंपरावादी)

◦ The definition given in the paper is the standard one-word-substitution clue for “orthodox”.

◦ Correct: He is an orthodox Hindu who performs every ritual exactly as prescribed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Prudent – acting with care and foresight; wise in practical matters.

• Compere – a person who introduces performers in a stage show; an anchor/host.

• Arsonist – a person who deliberately sets property on fire.

NOTE

• The printed word “conversational” is a typographical error for “conventional”; the intended answer remains Orthodox.

• Related one-word substitutions: Heterodox/Unorthodox – not conforming to accepted beliefs; Heretic – one who holds an opinion against established religion; Atheist – one who does not believe in God; Agnostic – one who believes God cannot be known.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

That were remarks made (in the heat of the moment).
option_1: At time when you cannot think carefully
option_4: To be dismissed from your job
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. At time when you cannot think carefully.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “in the heat of the moment” means while one is too angry or excited to think clearly. (आवेश में आकर / बिना सोचे‑समझे)

◦ It is used to excuse words or acts done impulsively under strong emotion.

◦ Correct: That were remarks made at a time when you cannot think carefully.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• “To exert all efforts” matches idioms like go all out / move heaven and earth.

• “To present a counter argument” matches to play devil’s advocate / to take issue with.

• “To be dismissed from your job” matches to get the sack / to be given marching orders.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: on the spur of the moment – suddenly, without planning; lose one’s cool – to get angry; fly off the handle – to lose temper suddenly.

• The printed “That were remarks” is the paper’s own wording and has been kept as it is.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Computers would replace the ______ technique of creating an image on paper, transferring it to transparent cells and again onto film.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. archaic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adjective describing a technique that computers would replace, i.e. an old, outdated technique.

◦ Archaic means very old, obsolete, no longer in use. (प्राचीन / अप्रचलित)

◦ Correct: Computers would replace the archaic technique of creating an image on paper…

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Assuage is a verb meaning to soothe or relieve; it cannot modify “technique”.

• Audacious means bold or daring – it does not fit a technique being replaced.

• Austere means severe, plain or without comfort – it does not convey “outdated”.

NOTE

• Synonyms of archaic: antiquated, obsolete, outmoded, primitive, old-fashioned.

• Antonyms of archaic: modern, contemporary, current, up-to-date, novel.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

A blessing in disguise
option_1: To have a dispute with someone
option_2: To go from being very poor to being very wealthy
option_3: A misfortune that unexpectedly turns into good fortune
option_4: Hear a good news after a long time
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A misfortune that unexpectedly turns into good fortune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A blessing in disguise means something that seems bad at first but later proves to be beneficial. (वरदान जो पहले अभिशाप लगे)

◦ The word disguise (भेस बदलना) itself signals that the good is hidden behind an apparent evil.

◦ Correct: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise – it led him to start his own firm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• “To have a dispute with someone” corresponds to to cross swords with / to be at loggerheads.

• “To go from being very poor to being very wealthy” corresponds to from rags to riches.

• “Hear a good news after a long time” has no standard idiom and is a distractor.

NOTE

• Related idioms: every cloud has a silver lining – every bad situation has some good in it; a mixed blessing – something with both advantages and drawbacks.

• Opposite idea: a Pyrrhic victory – a success that costs more than it is worth.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

I am thirty-two years old and my sister are fifteen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. my sister are fifteen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The rule of subject–verb agreement applies: a singular subject takes a singular verb.

◦ “My sister” is singular, so the verb must be is, not “are”. (कर्ता‑क्रिया समन्वय)

◦ Correct: I am thirty-two years old and my sister is fifteen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because the sentence clearly contains a verb-agreement error.

• Option 3 “years old and” is correct – age is expressed as “… years old”.

• Option 4 “I am thirty-two” is correct – “I” takes “am”.

NOTE

• With “each, every, either, neither, everyone, somebody” the verb is always singular.

• Two subjects joined by and take a plural verb (My sister and I are …), but subjects joined by or/nor agree with the nearer subject.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There's plenty here to trap the unwary and baffle even the ______ gambler!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. inveterate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires an adjective qualifying “gambler”; the contrast with “the unwary” demands a word meaning habitual/long-established.

◦ Inveterate means having a long-standing, deep-rooted habit. (आदी / पक्का)

◦ Correct: There’s plenty here to trap the unwary and baffle even the inveterate gambler!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Exenterate is a surgical verb meaning to remove the contents of an organ.

• Reiterate is a verb meaning to say something again for emphasis.

• Alliterate is a verb meaning to use the same initial sound in successive words.

NOTE

• Synonyms of inveterate: confirmed, habitual, chronic, ingrained, dyed-in-the-wool.

• Unwary = not cautious, easily deceived. (असावधान); Baffle = to puzzle or confuse. (चकरा देना)

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

It broke Eleanora's heart to see her daughter become that (wraith) of her former self.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Spirit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wraith (noun) means a ghost or a pale, shadowy figure, often used for someone reduced to a shadow of what they were. (प्रेत / छाया)

◦ Its closest synonym among the options is Spirit, which also denotes an apparition or ghost.

◦ Correct: It broke Eleanora’s heart to see her daughter become that spirit of her former self.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Wail – a long, loud cry of pain or grief; a sound, not a figure.

• Being – a living creature in general; too broad and lacks the ghostly sense.

• Yore – refers to time long past (“days of yore”); it is not a person.

NOTE

• Synonyms of wraith: phantom, apparition, spectre, shade, ghost.

• Common phrase: a shadow of one’s former self – much weaker or less impressive than before.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Desert
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Populate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As a verb, desert means to abandon or leave a place/person empty. (छोड़ देना / सुनसान कर देना)

◦ Populate means to fill a place with inhabitants, which is the exact opposite. (बसाना)

◦ Correct: The villagers deserted the area after the flood, and only years later did settlers populate it again.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Migrate – to move from one region to another; it involves leaving, so it is nearer in sense to desert, not opposite.

• Bereft – deprived of or lacking something; close to “deserted” in feeling.

• Forlorn – lonely and unhappy; again a synonym-side word.

NOTE

• Synonyms of desert (verb): abandon, forsake, maroon, jilt, defect.

• Do not confuse: desert (रेगिस्तान, noun), desert (त्यागना, verb) and dessert (मीठा व्यंजन, sweet dish).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Ram ran back to the / window to see the bars dangling / a few feet before the ground.
option_1: a few feet before the ground.
option_3: window to see the bars dangling
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a few feet before the ground.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is one of preposition. Bars hanging at a height are above the ground, not “before” the ground.

◦ Before shows time or order/priority, while above shows vertical position. (ऊपर / पहले)

◦ Correct: Ram ran back to the window to see the bars dangling a few feet above the ground.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is wrong because the sentence does contain a prepositional error.

• Option 3 “window to see the bars dangling” is correct – “to see” is an infinitive of purpose and “dangling” is a correct participle.

• Option 4 “Ram ran back to the” is correct – “ran back to” is standard.

NOTE

• above/over = higher than; below/under = lower than; before = earlier than / in front of in sequence.

• Dangle = to hang loosely and swing. (लटकना)

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Protesion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Protesion” is not an English word; the intended spelling is Protection (सुरक्षा) – the act of keeping someone or something safe.

◦ Words from “protect” keep the ‑ct‑ cluster: protect → protection, protective, protector.

◦ Correct: The fence was built for the protection of the crops.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Unshielded is correctly spelt – not covered or protected (un + shield + ed).

• Activity is correctly spelt – a thing that a person does; state of being active.

• Inactivity is correctly spelt – the state of doing nothing; idleness.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt ‑tion words in SSC: Occasion, Possession, Profession, Impression, Permission, Pronunciation, Maintenance, Committee.

• Remember: profession has ‑ss‑, but protection has ‑ct‑.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

(Because he has been in custody from last July,) Pickard will now be released in four months.
option_1: Because he had been under custody from last July,
option_2: Because he has been in custody since last July,
option_3: Because he had been in custody from last July,
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Because he has been in custody since last July,.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With the present perfect continuous/perfect tense, a point of time takes since, while a period of time takes for. “Last July” is a point of time, so since is required, not “from”. (निश्चित समय के लिए since)

◦ The correct collocation is in custody, not “under custody”.

◦ Correct: Because he has been in custody since last July, Pickard will now be released in four months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses the wrong preposition “under custody” and “from” instead of “since”.

• Option 3 uses the past perfect “had been”, which clashes with the future reference “will now be released”, and keeps “from”.

• Option 4 is wrong because the printed sentence does contain the error “from last July”.

NOTE

• since + point of time (since 2010, since Monday, since morning); for + length of time (for two hours, for ten years).

• Related collocations: in custody, in prison, in danger, in trouble, under arrest, under investigation.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

The dessert was not just extremely hot but (also to sweet as well).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. also too sweet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “not just … but also” is a correlative conjunction pair; the second half must begin with but also and nothing may be added after it.

◦ The printed “to” is a spelling error for too (= excessively), and “as well” is redundant with “also”. (एक ही अर्थ के दो शब्द एक साथ नहीं)

◦ Correct: The dessert was not just extremely hot but also too sweet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “besides too sweet as well.” breaks the “not just … but also” pair and repeats the idea twice.

• Option 2 is wrong because “to sweet as well” contains both a spelling error and redundancy.

• Option 3 “also being too sweet.” wrongly inserts “being”, destroying parallelism with the adjective “hot”.

NOTE

• Other correlative pairs: either … or, neither … nor, both … and, not only … but also, whether … or.

• Avoid double words: *also … as well*, *return back*, *repeat again*, *reason is because* are all redundancies.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Quiet and peaceful
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tranquil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tranquil is an adjective meaning calm, quiet and peaceful, free from disturbance. (शांत / स्थिर)

◦ It exactly matches the given group of words “Quiet and peaceful”.

◦ Correct: They spent the evening beside a tranquil lake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Introvert – a shy, reserved person who prefers solitude; it describes personality, not an atmosphere.

• Inundate – a verb meaning to flood or overwhelm.

• Incessant – continuing without pause; the very opposite of peaceful.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tranquil: serene, placid, calm, still, restful, undisturbed.

• Antonyms of tranquil: turbulent, agitated, tumultuous, noisy, restless.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Since these people used tobacco to ______ their deities, the herb itself was one of the instruments of godless, false religions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. propitiate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a verb that goes with “deities” in a religious offering context.

◦ Propitiate means to appease or win the favour of a god/person by doing something pleasing. (देवता को प्रसन्न करना)

◦ Correct: Since these people used tobacco to propitiate their deities…

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Expatiate – to speak or write at great length on a subject.

• Militate – (militate against) to be a powerful factor against something.

• Trace – to find or follow the course of something; meaningless with “deities” here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of propitiate: appease, placate, pacify, mollify, conciliate.

• Antonyms of propitiate: provoke, anger, enrage, antagonise.

• Deity = a god or goddess. (देवता)

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

An appeasements policies / were all but a sham to misdirect / the local groups.
option_2: were all but a sham to misdirect
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. An appeasements policies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article “An” is singular, but it is placed before the plural noun “policies” – a clear article–number clash.

◦ Also, a noun used as a modifier (appeasement policy) stays singular: “appeasement policies”, not “appeasements policies”.

◦ Correct: Appeasement policies were all but a sham to misdirect the local groups.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “the local groups.” is correct – “the” is fine before a plural noun.

• Option 2 “were all but a sham to misdirect” is correct – “all but” means “almost/virtually”.

• Option 4 is wrong because the sentence does contain an error in the first segment.

NOTE

• a/an are used only with singular countable nouns; plurals take the, some or no article.

• Attributive nouns stay singular: a five-year plan, a two-hour meeting, shoe shop, tooth brush.

• Sham = something that is not what it claims to be; a pretence. (ड्रामा / दिखावा)

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Apposite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Apposite (adjective) means very appropriate, apt and well suited to the occasion. (उपयुक्त / समीचीन)

◦ The spelling has a double ‑p‑ (ap-p-o-s-i-t-e) and a single ‑t‑.

◦ Correct: He made a few apposite remarks about the budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Apositte is wrong – it has a single ‑p‑ and a double ‑t‑.

• Aposire is wrong – no such word exists in English.

• Aposite is wrong – the required double ‑p‑ is missing.

NOTE

• Do not confuse apposite (apt) with opposite (contrary) or apposition (grammar: two nouns side by side).

• Synonyms of apposite: apt, pertinent, relevant, fitting, germane; Antonym: inapposite, irrelevant.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

You may wonder if anyone would (1) ______ to be diagnosed before they are even aware they have Alzheimer’s (2) ______? A recent survey shows that, indeed, they would. (3) ______ three-quarters of the respondents said they would want (4) ______ if they had Alzheimer’s disease, even if they were not yet experiencing (5) ______.

SubQuestion No : 21

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. want.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the modal “would”, so a bare infinitive (V1) is needed, and it must take the infinitive “to be diagnosed” after it.

◦ Want to be diagnosed = to wish to be told one has the disease – exactly the idea the passage explores, confirmed later by “they would want (4) ______”.

◦ Correct: You may wonder if anyone would want to be diagnosed before they are even aware they have Alzheimer’s disease.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• “drop to be diagnosed” is not an English structure; “drop” takes a gerund (drop doing).

• “surrender” means to give oneself up – illogical with “to be diagnosed”.

• “got” is a past form and cannot follow the modal “would”.

NOTE

• Modal + V1 always: would go, can play, must write, should read.

• Want is followed by a to-infinitive (want to know), never by a gerund.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

You may wonder if anyone would (1) ______ to be diagnosed before they are even aware they have Alzheimer’s (2) ______? A recent survey shows that, indeed, they would. (3) ______ three-quarters of the respondents said they would want (4) ______ if they had Alzheimer’s disease, even if they were not yet experiencing (5) ______.

SubQuestion No : 22

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. disease.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alzheimer’s is a degenerative brain disorder, and the standard collocation is Alzheimer’s disease. (अल्ज़ाइमर रोग)

◦ The same phrase “if they had Alzheimer’s disease” appears later in the passage, confirming the word.

◦ Correct: … before they are even aware they have Alzheimer’s disease?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• “health” would reverse the meaning – Alzheimer’s is an illness, not a state of health.

• “contamination” refers to pollution by an impurity; Alzheimer’s is not contagious or contaminating.

• “bug” is informal for a minor infection caused by germs, unsuitable for a degenerative disorder.

NOTE

• Diseases named after doctors keep the possessive: Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, Hodgkin’s lymphoma, Down’s syndrome.

• Diagnose = to identify an illness. (रोग की पहचान करना)

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

You may wonder if anyone would (1) ______ to be diagnosed before they are even aware they have Alzheimer’s (2) ______? A recent survey shows that, indeed, they would. (3) ______ three-quarters of the respondents said they would want (4) ______ if they had Alzheimer’s disease, even if they were not yet experiencing (5) ______.

SubQuestion No : 23

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nearly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank precedes the quantity “three-quarters of the respondents”, so it needs an adverb of approximation.

◦ Nearly means almost, not quite – the standard word used with survey figures. (लगभग)

◦ Correct: Nearly three-quarters of the respondents said they would want to know…

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Totally means completely; it cannot modify a fraction like “three-quarters”.

• Casually means in a relaxed or careless manner – it describes manner, not quantity.

• Firmly means in a strong, definite way – again an adverb of manner, not degree.

NOTE

• Adverbs of approximation used with statistics: nearly, almost, about, around, roughly, approximately, close to.

• Respondent = a person who answers a survey or questionnaire. (उत्तरदाता)

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

You may wonder if anyone would (1) ______ to be diagnosed before they are even aware they have Alzheimer’s (2) ______? A recent survey shows that, indeed, they would. (3) ______ three-quarters of the respondents said they would want (4) ______ if they had Alzheimer’s disease, even if they were not yet experiencing (5) ______.

SubQuestion No : 24

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to know.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb “want” is always followed by a to-infinitive, never by a gerund or a finite verb.

◦ Structure: want + to + V1 → “they would want to know”. (जानना चाहना)

◦ Correct: … three-quarters of the respondents said they would want to know if they had Alzheimer’s disease…

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• “knowing” is a gerund/participle – “want knowing” is ungrammatical.

• “knows” is a finite present-tense verb and cannot follow another verb directly.

• “known” is the past participle (V3) and needs an auxiliary such as “have/been”.

NOTE

• Verbs followed by to-infinitive: want, wish, hope, decide, agree, promise, refuse, expect, offer.

• Verbs followed by a gerund: enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, suggest, admit, consider, practise.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

You may wonder if anyone would (1) ______ to be diagnosed before they are even aware they have Alzheimer’s (2) ______? A recent survey shows that, indeed, they would. (3) ______ three-quarters of the respondents said they would want (4) ______ if they had Alzheimer’s disease, even if they were not yet experiencing (5) ______.

SubQuestion No : 25

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. symptoms.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is about a disease, so the outward signs of illness are called symptoms. (लक्षण)

◦ “Not yet experiencing symptoms” is the standard medical collocation for the pre-symptomatic stage.

◦ Correct: … even if they were not yet experiencing symptoms.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• “indexes” refers to alphabetical lists or numerical indicators – not used for illness.

• “evidences” is wrong here; evidence is an uncountable noun and belongs to legal/scientific proof.

• “marks” refers to visible spots or scores, not to the sensations of a disease.

NOTE

• Symptom = what the patient feels; sign = what the doctor observes.

• Uncountable nouns with no plural: evidence, information, advice, furniture, luggage, equipment, news.
